name: Whole-wheat Ragi Idli (2 pieces)
preparation_note: Steam with minimal rock salt (1/8 tsp per batch). Ragi provides high magnesium content critical for vasodilation. Serve with tomato chutney instead of coconut-based chutneys to avoid high sodium.

name: Oats Upma (1 cup)
preparation_note: Use rolled oats with 1/4 tsp rock salt maximum. Add fresh vegetables (tomato, onion, green peas). Avoid pre-packaged seasoning mixes which contain >300mg sodium per serving.

name: Fresh Tomato Chutney (high-lycopene)
preparation_note: Blend ripe tomatoes with green chilli, coriander, and minimal salt. High lycopene content reduces arterial stiffness. Preferred over coconut chutney (which adds 80–120mg Na per serving).

name: Brown Rice / Unpolished Red Rice (1 cup cooked)
preparation_note: Cook without added salt. The bran layer retains magnesium and B vitamins that support cardiovascular health. Glycaemic index is lower than white rice, reducing insulin spikes linked to hypertension.

name: Drumstick & Tomato Sambar (1 bowl ~200ml)
preparation_note: Strictly use 1/4 teaspoon salt for the entire batch (serves 4). Drumstick pods provide 120mg potassium per 100g. Avoid commercial sambar powder; use home-blended spices without added sodium. Toor dal provides plant-based protein without saturated fat.

name: Cabbage Poriyal (steamed, 1 cup)
preparation_note: Steam cabbage to preserve glucosinolates. Use mustard seeds, turmeric, and fresh shredded coconut. Add salt only at plating (reduces overall intake vs. cooking). Fiber content supports gut microbiome linked to BP regulation.

name: Multi-grain Chapati (2 pieces)
preparation_note: Blend wheat, ragi, and jowar flour in 2:1:1 ratio. Knead without salt; add 1/8 tsp per dough batch. Cook on dry pan. High magnesium from jowar supports smooth muscle relaxation in arterial walls.

name: Low-fat Curd Raita (1/2 cup)
preparation_note: Use low-fat curd (< 2% fat). Add grated cucumber, shredded beetroot, and minimal cumin. DASH recommends 2-3 dairy servings daily for calcium and potassium content. Probiotic content reduces systemic inflammation.

name: Ridge Gourd Kootu (Turai/Heerekai, 1 cup)
preparation_note: Pressure-cook ridge gourd with moong dal. Season with mustard, cumin, and fresh coconut. Ridge gourd is a natural diuretic (supports renal sodium excretion) and contains compounds that help relax arterial smooth muscle.

name: Fresh Banana (1 medium)
preparation_note: Ideal potassium supplement. A medium banana delivers 422mg K⁺ which directly counteracts sodium's blood-pressure-raising effect through the sodium-potassium pump. Best consumed post-meal or as afternoon snack.

name: Tender Coconut Water (200ml)
preparation_note: Fresh tender coconut water provides the highest natural potassium density of any common beverage (600mg/200ml). Rich in cytokinin compounds that have vasodilatory properties. Avoid packaged versions with added sodium or sugar.

name: Sprouted Moong Dal Soup (1 bowl)
preparation_note: Sprout moong dal for 24-48 hours to enhance bioavailability of magnesium and potassium. Cook lightly with turmeric and minimal salt. Folate content supports endothelial health.
